exeter.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of Exeter and Devon
s1loc: Exeter packs a real live-events calendar into a compact city. The Great Hall at the University of Exeter handles the big touring acts and orchestras, Exeter Phoenix runs as the city-centre multi-arts venue, the Corn Exchange takes comedy and tribute nights, and the Lemon Grove and Exeter Cavern carry the grassroots gig scene. A few miles south, Powderham Castle has become a major open-air concert and festival site, hosting summer headliners and the Tunes in the Castle weekend on its parkland.

And the trade runs at every size here. colchester.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of Colchester and Essex

Charter Hall is the city's multi-purpose room for live music, comedy and special events, the Mercury Theatre takes touring productions, and the small Headgate Theatre carries fringe and intimate shows. Through the summer, Castle Park becomes a major outdoor stage where thousands gather for headline concerts and the Colchester Food and Drink Festival. Between the halls, the theatres and the park, the city keeps stage, crew and front-of-house teams busy year-round.

As Britain's oldest recorded town and a new city, Colchester carries a busy heritage-events calendar. Colchester Castle and the Roman walls host outdoor history days, firstsite and the Colchester Arts Centre in the old St Mary-at-the-Wall church run year-round, and the University of Essex at Wivenhoe Park brings a steady student-gig scene, so production and front-of-house crews work right across the city through the season.

gateshead.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of the Tyne's south bank
s1loc: Gateshead anchors the live-music side of the Tyne. The Glasshouse International Centre for Music, the curved venue formerly known as Sage Gateshead, sits on the south bank as a home for everything from rock and pop gigs to the Royal Northern Sinfonia and the SummerTyne Americana Festival. Next door, the Baltic Centre for Contemporary Art and the wider quayside host open-air events and seasonal happenings, while Saltwell Park takes summer music days and the Enchanted Parks winter trail across its grounds.

And the trade runs at every size here. Major venues, festival operators and production companies field big crews and large seasonal teams and buy through procurement, while independent event crews, promoters and entertainers across Gateshead and the wider Tyneside scene need just a few branded pieces. Gateshead's own events spread well beyond the quayside. Gateshead International Stadium hosts major athletics meetings and outdoor concerts, Saltwell Park draws big community days, Trinity Square and the town centre run seasonal markets and live programmes, and the Angel of the North stands over it all as the region's landmark. Sitting across the Tyne from Newcastle, the town shares one of the busiest events calendars in the North East, so crews and front-of-house teams move between both banks through the year.

Gateshead's events reach goes wider still. The Gateshead Millennium Bridge and the quays host the region's big riverside celebrations and firework nights, while Dunston and the Team Valley anchor a busy outdoor and exhibition trade on the south bank. With NewcastleGateshead marketing one shared calendar across both sides of the Tyne, and the Baltic and the Glasshouse drawing year-round audiences, the town keeps stage, rigging and front-of-house crews moving through a packed programme from the river up to Low Fell across the year, alongside the seasonal markets and community days that fill its parks.
